metric.interpretation: For a zero-valued target, the uncapped fixed-scale error equals the absolute miss divided by one unit of that measure; it is not a conventional percentage relative to a nonzero target. The capped objective bounds each such contribution at 10.

source_code_evidence.finding: The numeric-fact validator rejects missing, invalid, or non-finite values; finite zero is accepted.
Identity references use the source numeric value.
The numeric value becomes the TargetSpec value.
Latest-observation selection can skip a zero only through the zero-as-missing helper.
The zero-as-missing helper applies only to specified CMS Medicaid roles, not IRS EITC.
EITC AGI-control uprating multiplies the source target value by a factor, preserving zero.
The all-return EITC uprating fallback also multiplies the target value by a factor, preserving zero.
Default fixed target scales use the absolute target with a one-unit floor.
The reported canonical objective caps scaled absolute errors before averaging.
The optimization loss applies the same cap using torch.clamp.

conclusions.interpretation: The feed declares numeric observations equal to zero. Available metadata does not establish whether those zeros reflect the substantive source data or an extraction/source-data issue. They must not be described as suppressed or missing on this evidence.
conclusions.deduction: Capped-fit improvement can coexist with higher uncapped error because errors beyond the cap make equal contributions to the fitted objective. This alone does not establish more accurate EITC estimation.
conclusions.target_handling: All targets remain unchanged across the designs in this run.
